claims.text: A DNN interatomic potential trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations will be a superior thermodynamic-integration reference to traditional EAM potentials.
The DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM references.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-melting alloys, including refractory high-entropy alloys, in both solid and liquid states.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9Tm to Tm.
The DNN should be trained on extensive ab initio data spanning the wide array of liquid atomic configurations.
The trained DNN should replace the EAM reference in a TOR-TILD-style thermodynamic-integration protocol.
A DNN potential can describe structural behavior in both solid and liquid high-entropy materials near melting.
The proposed simulations or experiments should be conducted at around 0.9–1.0Tm in controlled atmospheres.
The DNN will capture both short- and long-range atomic correlations in the liquid.
Capturing liquid correlations will improve the representation of local atomic configurations.
Improved representation of local configurations will produce a smoother and more continuous energy landscape between the reference and ab initio target states.
Training on varied ab initio liquid configurations will make the DNN reproduce the target ab initio potential-energy surface more faithfully.
The DNN reference will significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reduced path mismatch will lower the statistical error of calculated free energies.
Reduced path mismatch will improve the accuracy of predicted thermodynamic properties.
TOR-TILD EAM references have insufficient phase-space overlap because they cannot adequately represent the diverse configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The benefit of the DNN reference may diminish for simpler systems or at temperatures far below melting.
The magnitude of the expected mismatch reduction is uncertain because prior elemental and binary benchmarks are limited.
